=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1684-1685 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: An unterminated `##[group]Run` header causes `_strip_step_env_values` to discard all buffered lines and emit the omission marker, even when no `env:` block was entered, losing nonsensitive diagnostic output and reporting an env omission where none occurred.
  WHY: Existing intake fixtures and CI tests lose diagnostic evidence; production heal diagnosis can lose actionable log content, though openai_gpt-6-luna recommends closing completed-log fixtures instead of changing the filtering behavior; severity is critical, with four reviewers rating it BLOCKER and one rating it MAJOR.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:300 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_STEP_HEADER_KEY_RE` recognizes only `shell:`, `with:`, and `env:` as header boundaries, so other standard step keys inside an env block may be treated as env entries and redacted.
  WHY: A key such as `continue-on-error:` or `name:` can be replaced wholesale with `[redacted]`, losing the key and its value.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1684-1685 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The unterminated-header branch drops the env name as well as its value, contrary to the documented contract that preserves each name and redacts its value.
  WHY: The resulting evidence does not identify which environment variable was redacted, and the existing regression test asserts that the name is absent.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_SECRET_PATTERNS | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The secret-redaction patterns may be incomplete and may cause false positives or miss credential variations.
  WHY: The reviewer could not establish that the patterns cover all relevant variations, so credentials may leak or nonsensitive output may be redacted.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1914 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The case-insensitive authorization pattern changes filtered output, but the changelog fragment and `_SECRET_PATTERNS` docstring do not document that behavior change.
  WHY: A downstream test or contract asserting the previous output may fail when an authorization value is now replaced with `[redacted]`.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: Retain environment variable names while redacting their values, as promised by the docstring.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1684-1685 (`if in_header: kept.append(_STEP_ENV_UNTERMINATED_MARKER)`) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_strip_step_env_values` drops all buffered `header_lines` when a `##[group]Run` header lacks a closing `##[endgroup]`, regardless of whether an `env:` block was entered.
  WHY: The `JOB_LOG` fixture (line 1645) and `PLAN_JOB_LOG` fixture (line 4956) have no `env:` block, yet their diagnostic lines are replaced by the marker, causing three CI tests to fail and production diagnosis to lose actionable content.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The linked issue #6640 (re-issue of #6459) requires "Omit environment values from agent-readable logs and redact Basic authorization headers before writing evidence; fail closed when sensitive log fields cannot be safely reduced."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py in `_strip_step_env_values` lines 1684-1685
  Evidence of absence: The fail-closed behavior is applied too broadly to unterminated `##[group]Run` headers without an `env:` block, discarding non-env diagnostic output and causing three CI failures.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_STEP_HEADER_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:shell|with|env):(?:\s|$)") | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The header-boundary regex recognizes only `shell:`, `with:`, and `env:`.
  WHY: Other standard keys after `env:` may leave `in_env` true, causing incorrect processing of subsequent lines or preventing sensitive data from being redacted.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_SECRET_PATTERNS | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The secret patterns may be incomplete despite the added case-insensitive authorization pattern.
  WHY: Redaction may miss credential variations or unnecessarily redact nonsensitive output.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_strip_step_env_values (lines 1643-1710) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: An unclosed `##[group]Run` header causes the function to discard buffered lines, including diagnostic information outside an `env:` block.
  WHY: Existing CI tests and legitimate truncated logs lose error lines and step output because any unterminated header is treated as a redaction failure.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:test_intake_opens_upstream_hotfix_issue_for_workflow_defect, test_autofix_intake_reads_successful_review_job_when_no_job_failed | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Test assertions fail because log content is redacted or truncated.
  WHY: The test suite expects diagnostic lines from job logs to verify heal behavior, but the log processing masks or removes them.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The implementation must redact credentials and environment values from agent-readable logs and redact Basic authorization headers before writing evidence, while failing closed when sensitive log fields cannot be safely reduced.
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_strip_step_env_values` and `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py`
  Evidence of absence: The implementation loses non-env diagnostic content when a header is truncated and does not update the existing test suite, leaving CI in a broken state.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: lines 1643-1686 (`_strip_step_env_values`); specifically lines 1684-1685 (`if in_header: kept.append(_STEP_ENV_UNTERMINATED_MARKER)`) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Any unterminated `##[group]Run` header causes all buffered `header_lines` to be discarded, regardless of whether an `env:` block was entered.
  WHY: `JOB_LOG` (lines 1645-1650) and `PLAN_JOB_LOG` (lines 4956-4961) contain diagnostic content without an `env:` block; filtering removes it, leaving intake prompts with only the marker and causing CI failures.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: lines 1684-1685; comparison with the documented env-entry contract at lines 1632-1634 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The unterminated-header branch drops the env name as well as its value, contrary to the documented promise that each `NAME: value` entry keeps its name and gets `[redacted]` for its value.
  WHY: Operators cannot see which env var was redacted, and `test_filter_log_drops_unterminated_step_header` asserts `"TOKEN" not in filtered`, locking in the behavior.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: line 300 (`_STEP_HEADER_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:shell|with|env):(?:\s|$)")`) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The pattern recognizes only `shell:`, `with:`, and `env:` as header-section boundaries, so other step keys inside an env block are not treated as boundaries.
  WHY: A line such as `continue-on-error:` or `name:` can be rejected as an env entry and replaced wholesale, losing the key and its value.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: lines 1684-1685 (terminal condition); contrast with `_STEP_ENV_UNTERMINATED_MARKER` definition at line 304 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The unterminated-header marker is emitted for every unterminated `##[group]Run` block, including blocks with no `env:` section.
  WHY: Operators see an env omission marker for a truncation that did not involve an env block, making the marker misleading.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: line 1914 (the `authorization\s*:\s*` pattern; comment at 1913 explicitly says "HTTP header names are case-insensitive (`curl -v` prints `authorization:`)") | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The case-insensitive authorization pattern changes which inputs are rewritten to `[redacted]`, but the changelog fragment and `_SECRET_PATTERNS` docstring do not call out the behavior change.
  WHY: A downstream test or contract that expected the previous literal value may fail when the authorization line is redacted.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Omit environment values from agent-readable logs and redact Basic authorization headers before writing evidence; fail closed when sensitive log fields cannot be safely reduced." Retain useful nonsensitive evidence when a job log ends mid-step.
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_strip_step_env_values` lines 1643-1686
  Evidence of absence: The fail-closed mechanism drops every buffered line for any unterminated `##[group]Run` header, including diagnostic output; this breaks the three named intake tests and can hide error lines used for heal-issue classification.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Redact environment values from agent-readable logs and redact Basic authorization headers before writing evidence; fail closed when sensitive log fields cannot be safely reduced." Preserve useful nonsensitive evidence and environment variable names.
  Expected change site: tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py
  Evidence of absence: `test_filter_log_drops_unterminated_step_header` (lines 750-770) asserts that `TOKEN` is absent, contradicting the retention clause and the docstring contract that env names are preserved; `test_intake_opens_upstream_hotfix_issue_for_workflow_defect` (line 1775), `test_autofix_intake_reads_successful_review_job_when_no_job_failed` (line 2095), and `test_intake_phase_failure_opens_issue_from_the_failed_job_log` (line 4989) rely on diagnostics surviving into the prompt.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
